title: Elihu
lead: Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite is the young man who speaks four times after Job and his three friends fall silent (Job 32–37). He is not mentioned before or after: the prologue does not name him, and the LORD's verdict on the friends (Job 42:7–9) leaves him out. Readers have seen him as a later addition, a pompous youth the book mocks, a true forerunner of God's speeches, and a prophet. Several other men in the Bible share the name, which means "He is my God."

sections.b: The name, a form of Elijah's, belongs also to an ancestor of Samuel (1 Samuel 1:1), a commander from Manasseh who joined David (1 Chronicles 12:20), a gatekeeper (1 Chronicles 26:7), and a brother of David who led the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 27:18). None of them is connected with Job's Elihu.
